posts.text:
It is very clear that This Time is Different in terms of AI compared to previous innovations.

That doesn't mean it differs in every way from past technologies (the s-curve of diffusion is a surprisingly universal finding), but it differs in many ways that make applying old patterns hard.

posts.text:
Existential AI risk is obviously critical, but it is not the only AI thing that requires policy.

I worry it will become the sole focus of AI discussions. We don’t need better models for AI to have wide impacts on jobs & society and we need to be preparing to encourage good outcomes & mitigate bad.

It is very clear that This Time is Different in terms of AI compared to previous innovations.

That doesn't mean it differs in every way from past technologies (the s-curve of diffusion is a surprisingly universal finding), but it differs in many ways that make applying old patterns hard.

There seems to be a persistent belief that frontier AI companies are unprofitable serving models but it appears that Anthropic has 80%+ gross margins on inference. Training for new models are where most of the costs are. www.ft.com/content/4564...

This work is important regardless of existential risk, and needs a lot more focus.

I wrote about one set of approaches to the problem (The Twilight Factory), but there are others. www.oneusefulthing.org/p/agency-and...

Those effects will not be all at once, but the fact that change will occur is inevitable now. But inevitable change does not mean the type of change is inevitable. It is increasingly important that we develop & share models of AI-human work that enhance, rather than only replace, human labor.

I cannot emphasize enough how much GPT-6 Astra and Fable 5.1 are already enough for transformative impact in large sections of the economy. They can reliably do weeks worth of human work when properly guided & harnessed.

Existential AI risk is obviously critical, but it is not the only AI thing that requires policy.

I worry it will become the sole focus of AI discussions. We don’t need better models for AI to have wide impacts on jobs & society and we need to be preparing to encourage good outcomes & mitigate bad.
